title: Estimating the mean from grouped data

accuracy.evidence: Checked on 26 Nov 2026 against DfE GCSE Mathematics subject content (2013) S3/S4 (grouped frequency tables; 'interpret, analyse and compare ... measures of central tendency, including modal class'), the AQA 8300 specification note on estimating the mean from grouped data using midpoints, and the KS3 Statistics programme of study. Every number was recomputed in code (GME.N, SUM, EST, cum, medClass, modal, trueMean in gmean_art.js): f 2, 5, 6, 12, 5 give n 30; midpoints 135-175; f x midpoint 270, 725, 930, 1980, 875, total 4780; estimate 159.33 (159.3 to 1 d.p.); running totals 2, 7, 13, 25, 30 so the 15th and 16th values are in 160-170; modal class 160-170; true mean 157.73 with the 12 pupils at 161 cm and 160.93 at 169 cm; Show me sandbox data 0, 0, 2, 6, 12 gives 170.0 and 12, 6, 2, 0, 0 gives 140.0; every parameterised item checked at its corners.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented grouped-data slips (Watson and Moritz 2000 on rote mean calculation; GCSE examiner reports on grouped means): using a class boundary or the class width (step 1 prediction options '150, where the class starts' and '10, the class width', boundary-specific canvas feedback, challenge tags 'bound' and 'width'); dividing by the number of classes or stopping at the total (step 2 prediction, the DIV replies that show 956 cm and 478 cm are impossible, tag 'rows'); believing the estimate is exact (step 3 slider, tag 'exact'); giving a frequency as the modal class (tag 'freq'); taking the middle row as the median class (step 4 prediction and feedback, tag 'middle'); accepting an estimate outside the range (tag 'range').

lab_distinct.evidence: The mechanism is grouped data itself: a pin snapped to 5 cm on a 130-180 cm number line with five class boxes (so boundaries and midpoints are the only choices), a grouped table with a midpoint column, a slider that moves the 12 pupils inside one class while the true mean and the fixed midpoint estimate are drawn on a second axis, a histogram with running totals for the modal and median class, and draggable histogram bars with the estimate on a cm axis. flag_freqavg works with ungrouped values (mode cell, middle place, f x x); the lab_distinct gate passes.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners discover that a boundary is a poor stand-in from the feedback, see 4780 divided by 5 or 10 give impossible heights, and then see directly why the answer is an estimate: moving the 12 pupils from 161 to 169 cm moves the true mean from 157.7 to 160.9 cm while the estimate stays at 159.3 cm. The running total shows the median class is not the middle row, and reshaping the histogram shows how heavily filled classes pull the estimate and that it cannot leave the 130-180 cm range.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option that the lab then disproves: '150, where the class starts' or '10, the class width' (the midpoint step), '5, the number of classes' (the divisor gives 956 cm), 'Higher than the estimate' or 'Exactly the same' when the pupils sit at 161 cm (the true mean falls to 157.7 cm), and '150 <= h < 160, the middle row' for the median class (the running total reaches only 13 there).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with answers in rotating positions; every wrong option carries a slip tag with its own message: 'bound' (that is a class boundary), 'width' (that is the class width), 'rows' (divide by the total frequency, not the number of classes, and do not stop at the total), 'exact' (the real values are unknown), 'freq' (that is a frequency, not a class), 'middle' (the middle row is not special), 'range' (a mean lies between the smallest and largest values).

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py passes with the learner audience; the kid text scores about FK grade 4.7 (target 6.5) and the adult text about 8.5 (target 9.5). Curriculum terms (class, class boundary, midpoint, total frequency, modal class, median class, running total) are each explained where first used, and canvas instructions are one line per step.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one step: what a class holds, choosing the midpoint, f x midpoint divided by total frequency with a sense check, why it is an estimate plus modal and median class. The adult notes give curriculum references, the exact worked numbers, named mistakes with a source, and what the lab does. The filler gate passes.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at iPhone 13 (390 px) in light and dark and on desktop for every step before and after Show me, plus canvas tap and drag tests on a phone viewport. Fixes made from screenshots: the number line and the class slider jumped when a reply line appeared (now fixed heights), the step 1 footnote was clipped (now wraps), the table header 'Midpoint' and 'f x mid' overlapped (columns moved), the step 3 estimate and midpoint labels collided (moved apart), and the step 5 checklist overlapped the axis (histogram shortened).

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin with a descriptive aria-label ('Use 155 cm to stand for the class 150 <= h < 160', 'Work out f times midpoint for 160 <= h < 170', 'Divide the total by 30 pupils', 'Move all 12 pupils to the shortest end, 161 cm', 'Median class: 160 <= h < 170', 'Move one pupil from the shortest filled class up one class'); the canvas aria-label updates live with each reply; the challenge uses real buttons and a polite live region; axe WCAG 2.1 AA runs in both themes in the browser gate.

sources: DfE (2013) GCSE Mathematics subject content and assessment objectives, Statistics S3 and S4 (grouped data, modal class, measures of central tendency)
AQA GCSE Mathematics (8300) specification, S4: estimating the mean from grouped data using midpoints
DfE (2013) National Curriculum in England: mathematics programmes of study, Key Stage 3 Statistics
Watson, J. M. and Moritz, J. B. (2000) The longitudinal development of understanding of average. Mathematical Thinking and Learning 2(1-2), 11-50
